question.text: A portfolio has 60% in a bond returning 7% and 40% in a bond returning 9%. The weighted-average portfolio return is:

explanation.text: The Logic: Source p.146 supports computing portfolio return as the weighted average of constituent returns: 0.6*7% + 0.4*9% = 4.2% + 3.6% = 7.8%. The Trap: A simple average ignores the 60/40 weights and overstates the contribution of the 9% bond. Note: Source p.64 gives the definition of YTM; the weighted-average formula on p.146 is the general portfolio-return rule applied here.
